title: Historical Investigative Records / Cross-Shared New York State Police Intelligence

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

TARGET SUBJECT: Stefano Magaddino (Date of Birth: October 14, 1891 | Date of Death: July 19, 1974)
LOCATION OF RECORDS: FBI Headquarters & FBI Buffalo Field Office

To Whom It May Concern,

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552). 

I am requesting copies of all historical investigative files, intelligence briefs, memos, and indexed records maintained by the FBI Headquarters and the Buffalo Field Office concerning Stefano Magaddino, specifically covering the timeframe of 1957 through 1970.

I specifically request the inclusion of all cross-shared intelligence, logs, transcripts, translations, and summaries provided to the FBI by the New York State Police Bureau of Criminal Investigation (BCI) / "Forest Avenue" undercover squad in Buffalo, New York working as an intelligence unit for the New York State Police. The "Forest Avenue Boys" were the NYSP department's precursor to their New York State Police Organized Crime Task Force. 

Because the subject, Stefano Magaddino, passed away in 1974, individual privacy exemptions under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(7)(C) no longer apply. 

In addition to conducting this search for records at the FBI Field Office in Buffalo, NY, please conduct an additional search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies at FBI Headquarters. 

Please also conduct a search for records at the Alexandria Records Center.

If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records.

If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

FEE WAIVER REQUEST:
I request a waiver of all search and duplication fees because the disclosure of this information is in the public interest. It is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the historical operations of organized crime and mid-century law enforcement coordination in Western New York. These records are strictly for historical research purposes and not for commercial use.

If this request is denied in whole or in part, please justify all deletions by reference to specific exemptions of the Act. Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Mob

title: Public Records Request – 2026 Massachusetts SUN Bucks Incident (Department Of Elementary And Secondary Education)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Dear Records Access Officer:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I am requesting electronic records concerning the 2026 Massachusetts SUN Bucks (Summer EBT) fraud/theft incident.

For the period April 1, 2026 through the present, please provide records in your agency's possession concerning:

Prior warnings or vulnerabilities: Alerts, warnings, reports, or communications received from USDA/FNS, other states, law enforcement, EBT vendors/processors, or other agencies concerning SUN Bucks/Summer EBT theft, skimming, compromised cards, or related security vulnerabilities.
Detection and response: Records showing when Massachusetts first became aware of suspicious or unauthorized 2026 SUN Bucks transactions, how the activity was detected, and actions taken in response.
Agency communications/referrals: Communications, notifications, or referrals concerning the incident between your agency and DTA, EOHHS, DESE, the Governor's Office, USDA/FNS, USDA-OIG, the U.S. Attorney's Office, FBI, HSI, law enforcement, EBT processors/vendors, or other governmental entities.
Scope of the incident: Records showing the number and dollar value of fraudulent transactions, affected cards or households, geographic or retailer-level summaries, and amounts recovered, reversed, replaced, or remaining as losses.
Card issuance/security: Records concerning security risks associated with loading 2026 SUN Bucks benefits onto previously issued cards, including any risk assessment or discussion of compromised cards, PINs, card replacement, or other safeguards.
Post-incident findings: Incident reports, investigative summaries, after-action reviews, findings, recommendations, corrective-action plans, or records documenting security or policy changes made or proposed following the incident.

I am not requesting recipient names, card numbers, PINs, or other personally identifying information. Aggregate or redacted records are acceptable.

Please provide responsive records electronically. If records are withheld or redacted, please identify the applicable exemption and provide all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions.

If this request is expected to result in substantial fees, please provide an estimate before processing and advise whether the request can be narrowed to reduce those costs.

Thank you.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Susanne Cleveland

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

concerning Thomas Andrew Lehrer (born April 9, 1928, New York, New York; died July 26, 2025), the mathematician and satirical songwriter, who served at the National Security Agency as a U.S. Army enlisted soldier from approximately 1955 to 1957:
1.	Mr. Lehrer's personnel security file, clearance and indoctrination records, and any records of his security debriefing upon departure from the Agency in 1957.
2.	Any foreign travel notifications, pre-travel briefings, or post-travel debriefings, and any records of foreign contacts, concerning Mr. Lehrer during his service or in connection with any post-1957 access, consulting, or Agency contact.
3.	Any Office of Security, counterintelligence, or personnel records concerning Mr. Lehrer, including any records generated by his public performances, publications, or political activity during or after his service.
4.	Any records held by the Center for Cryptologic History, the Agency's oral history program, or its historical files that mention Mr. Lehrer.
Please search historical and Center for Cryptologic History holdings as well as personnel security records, since historical files on notable former personnel are frequently retained after personnel records are destroyed.

Mr. Lehrer is deceased, which substantially diminishes the personal privacy interests protected by Exemptions 6 and 7(C). A copy of the obituary is attached.
If any responsive records have been transferred to another agency or to the National Archives, please identify the recipient. If any responsive records were destroyed, please state the records-disposition authority under which they were destroyed and the date of destruction.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.
I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Illinois SoS Plate Watch Hotline Reports and Outcomes
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

This request concerns the Secretary of State's Plate Watch Hotline, announced October 22, 2025. "Report" means any complaint or tip submitted to (312) 814-1730 or platewatch@ilsos.gov, including voicemails, call notes, and email attachments. I am requesting any records from September 1, 2025 through the date of your search. 

I do not seek private information as defined in 5 ILCS 140/2(c-5), or the name or contact information of any complainant, witness, or other third party. The Office may redact that information. I ask that the following remain visible in each report: the date, the location, the vehicle description, the alleged violation, and the issuing state of any license plate.

If the Office claims an exemption for records under one item, please release the records responsive to the others.

1. Any existing record that states a count or tally of reports received, investigated, closed, or open; of registrations or plates suspended or revoked; or of citations, warnings, or referrals issued. Examples include status reports, briefing memos, and statistics prepared for the Secretary or the press office. If no such record exists, the Office may instead provide a query result stating these figures. Data fields in a public body's database are public records, and extracting them does not create a new record. 5 ILCS 140/2(c); Hites v. Waubonsee Community College, 2016 IL App (2d) 150836.
2. Any log or spreadsheet the Office uses to track reports and their handling. If the Office tracks reports in a database or case management system, I request the data in these fields for each report: date received; channel (phone or email); location; alleged violation; status; disposition; any agency to which the report was referred; and date closed. Data fields in a public body's database are public records, and extracting them does not create a new record. 5 ILCS 140/2(c); Hites v. Waubonsee Community College, 2016 IL App (2d) 150836. If the Office keeps no such log or database, I will accept a summary showing the same information for each report, current to within 30 days of your response.
3. Letters and notices the Office sent to any rental car, leasing, or fleet company, any federal agency, or any registered vehicle owner about alleged or suspected license plate tampering by federal agents, including warning letters, cease-and-desist letters, and notices suspending or revoking any vehicle registration or registration plate; any written response the Office received; and records of any resulting administrative hearing. The Office has previously released some of these records under FOIA.
4. Each report that led to a warning, citation, referral, suspension, or revocation, with the record of its disposition. If the Office withholds any of these records under section 7(1)(d), please identify the proceeding or investigation at issue and explain how release of the redacted record would interfere with it, consistent with the detailed factual basis that 5 ILCS 140/9(a) and (b) require.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Please provide records in their original electronic format where available, or, where electronic records are unavailable or impracticable, as searchable PDFs.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

HCvP
